articles.headline: NFL Week 3: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday's games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 3.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第3週：日曜日の試合の要点、疑問点、ファンタジーの視点
articles.descriptionJa: NFL Nationの取材記者がすべての試合に反応し、日曜日の各試合から浮き彫りになった最大の疑問に答えます。第3週から分かったことは以下の通りです。
articles.body:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season featured shocking performances in the early window Sunday, including another  turnover-filled afternoon by Patriots quarterback Drake Maye and a three-touchdown performance by Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs. Commanders backup quarterback Marcus Mariota also led the team to a huge upset over the Seahawks.

Elsewhere during the early window, the Steelers got the best of a shootout versus the Bengals. The Giants defeated the Titans without starting quarterback Jaxson Dart, while the Browns won their second straight game.

In the late window, the 49ers defeated the Cardinals despite a late comeback attempt. And quarterback Kyler Murray beat the Bucs in his first full game with the Vikings.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

Jump to:

MIN-TB | ARI-SF

SEA-WSH | CAR-CLE | CIN-PIT

TEN-NYG | LAC-BUF | HOU-IND

NYJ-DET | NE-JAX | KC-MIA

Catch up on Thursday's game:

ATL-GB

Minnesota 23, Tampa Bay 16

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Vikings

Can WR Jordan Addison fill in for Justin Jefferson? Nope. And that's not intended to insult Addison, who is a very talented WR2. But Jefferson, who left in the first quarter because of an ankle injury, is one of the best players in the NFL. Addison made several acrobatic catches, including a 30-yard reception along the sideline and a 41-yard touchdown. But to this point in his career, he has not been a receiver that opponents need to design their game plan around.

What to make of the QB performance: Kyler Murray's first full game of his Vikings tenure was rocky to say the least. He found Addison on those two big plays, but otherwise, the Vikings couldn't move the ball after Jefferson departed. At one point, Murray completed only 2 of 15 passes. The Vikings barely had more first downs (nine) than punts (eight). -- Kevin Seifert

Next game: vs. Dolphins (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Buccaneers

Is there any hope of this getting better? The defense holding a Jefferson-less Vikings to three points in the second half gave them a chance, but what the offense is doing is unsustainable. Quarterback Baker Mayfield, who missed the final drive after injuring his thumb, was sacked six times, and the offense went just 2-of-13 on third down. That made it incredibly difficult to climb out of a 10-0 hole.

What to make of the QB performance: The Mayfield (17 for 34, 217 passing yards) to rookie Ted Hurst III connection showed improvement with a 40-yard touchdown in the first quarter, but a Luke Goedeke holding call wiped out Chris Godwin Jr.'s would-be score later on. And of course, there was that fourth-quarter pick which brought Mayfield's turnover total to five this season. -- Jenna Laine

articles.headline: NFL Week 3: Wild stats on the Texans, Saints, Chargers, more
articles.description: Coaching decisions costing the Texans? Milestones for a Commanders LB and Raiders-Saints TEs? A balanced Steelers offense? And the Chargers losing with five takeaways?
articles.headlineJa: NFL第3週：テキサンズ、セインツ、チャージャーズなどの驚くべき記録
articles.descriptionJa: コーチ陣の決断がテキサンズの勝敗に影響？コマンダーズのLBやレイダース／セインツのTEが節目の記録を達成？バランスの取れたスティーラーズの攻撃？そしてチャージャーズが5つのテイクアウェイを奪いながら敗れた理由とは？
articles.body:
If you had the Raiders at 3-0 and Texans at 0-3 after three weeks, good on you. The NFL is always wacky in September -- and never wackier than when Marcus Mariota leads the Commanders to a win over the Super Bowl champion Seahawks.

Every Sunday, I'll find several of the coolest advanced stats from the day's NFL action to share with you -- stats to explain all the action and what it means. Some call them NFL Next Gen Stats. I call them Next Ben Stats: the data that might not make it on the broadcast but will make you a smarter fan (and laugh a little bit, probably).

Let's start Week 3's list with coaching mistakes that might have cost the Texans a much-needed divisional win.

Jump to an eye-popping stat on:

Texans decisions | Jones up the middle

Rodgers time to pass | Styles impact

Chargers takeaways | Raiders-Saints TEs

3.6%: How much win probability the Texans lost when they kicked a field goal fourth-and-4

That was via ESPN's model. The NFL Next Gen Stats model was even worse at 5.5%.

The Texans are 0-3 for a lot of reasons, and clock and game management is a solid chunk of it. This particular fourth down came with Houston losing 16-7 with 7:36 remaining. The Texans knew they'd need a touchdown to get back into it but elected to instead kick the field goal from inside the 10-yard line.

It looked like it worked out. Houston forced a fumble on the ensuing drive, then scored the go-ahead touchdown with Woody Marks. But with the score at 17-16, all the Colts needed to get back on top was a field goal. They ultimately got it to go ahead 19-17. But that wasn't the real concerning part -- it's how much clock Houston coach DeMeco Ryans let run on Indy's drive before using his timeouts. After a first-and-10 run of 5 yards from Jonathan Taylor, the clock rolled from 1:04 to 0:29 (and an expiring play clock) ... and then Ryans called the timeout. Houston would lose 19-17 after getting the ball back with just 11 seconds on the clock.

This isn't the first questionable fourth-down call for Ryans. He opted to kick a field goal on fourth-and-1 from the Bengals' 40 in last week's loss, a decision that cost him 7.4% in win probability. In both the Bengals game and the Colts game, an early fourth-down run was stuffed, and those failures seem to cut Ryans' confidence in fourth-down decisions at the knees. It's often the case that defensive-minded head coaches default to punts and field goals, but in the case of a struggling offense like the Texans' unit, it's even more important to go for fourth downs when near the end zone -- you're unlikely to keep getting back there!

198: How many passing yards Daniel Jones had between the numbers

Consider that he only had 235 passing yards altogether in the win over Houston. Here are the overall numbers throwing to the middle of the field: 20-for-25, 198 yards and one touchdown. articles.headline: 'Not my concern': Ex-Man City boss Mancini brushes off guilty reports
articles.description: Roberto Mancini brushed off reports that his former club Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of financial breaches allegedly committed during his time in charge of the club.
articles.headlineJa: 「自分には関係ない」元マンC監督のマンチーニ氏、有罪報道を一蹴
articles.descriptionJa: ロベルト・マンチーニ氏は、自身が指揮を執っていた期間に犯したとされる財務違反について、古巣のマンチェスター・シティがプレミアリーグから有罪と認定されたとする報道を一蹴しました。
articles.body:
Roberto Mancini brushed off reports that his former club Manchester City have been found guilty by the Premier League of financial breaches allegedly committed during his time as manager.

A source confirmed to ESPN on Friday that City were expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of 115 charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

- Man City verdict will leave a stain and stench on a Premier League era

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

- Returning Mancini accepts fans' jeers as Italy beaten by Belgium

Among the alleged breaches cited by the Premier League in 2023 were that City had failed to provide "full details of manager remuneration in its relevant contracts with its manager" between 2009 and 2013, the period in which Mancini was in charge and delivered City's first title in 44 years.

According to German publication Der Spiegel, Mancini is said to have at one point earned £1.45 million in a basic salary and £1.75 million as a consultant for a team controlled by City owner Sheikh Mansour in Abu Dhabi.

But speaking at a news conference in Türkiye on Sunday, the now-Italy coach questioned the reported verdict and said it was a matter for the club, not him.

"It's not an issue that concerns me," he said in Bursa ahead of Monday's UEFA Nations League fixture. "It's nothing new because this matter has been discussed for the last four or five years.

"Manchester City has not been found guilty, and the alleged double contract is not my concern. It's their issue, not mine."

In a statement on Friday, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

In his own statement on Saturday, Man City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak said "nothing has changed" regarding the case, adding "our confidence and intent in proving the club's innocence is just as strong as when this began."

As well as the 2011-12 Premier League title, Mancini also led Man City to victory in the 2011 FA Cup final during his four seasons at the helm. 

He returned to take charge of Italy for a second time this summer.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Aaron Rodgers' 2026 NFL season: Tracking records, milestones
articles.description: The Steelers QB, who is in his 22nd NFL season, is chasing records, and ESPN is chronicling his "last rodeo."
articles.headlineJa: アーロン・ロジャースの2026年NFLシーズン：記録達成とマイルストーンを追う
articles.descriptionJa: NFL22シーズン目を迎えたスティーラーズのQBは記録達成に挑んでおり、ESPNは彼の「ラスト・ロデオ（最後の挑戦）」を追跡取材しています。
articles.body:
Entering his 22nd NFL season -- or as Aaron Rodgers says, "his last rodeo" -- the 42-year-old Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is on the cusp of joining several exclusive clubs as he moves up the ranks in the league record books.

In 2025, he passed former teammate Brett Favre to take sole possession of fourth place in career touchdown passes thrown with his 509th TD pass in the Week 3 win against the New England Patriots.

"Every now and then I made some special throws that led to touchdowns, but I've been playing a long time, and it's a longevity thing," Rodgers said before passing Favre's mark last season. "I'm proud of it, but not a big deal."

Rodgers also went on to supplant Ben Roethlisberger for fifth in all-time passing yards in the second quarter of the Thursday night loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Oct. 16, 2025.

That Rodgers is still chasing records in 2026 is somewhat of a surprise after he suggested at times during the 2025 season that he was nearing the end of his career.

"It's the twilight of my career," he said after beating the Minnesota Vikings in Ireland on Oct. 5, 2025. "I used to say five, six, seven years ago, I was on the back nine. But I'm teeing off on 18 right now."

In that win, Rodgers made two more noteworthy entries into the record books: most completions of 50-plus yards and second quarterback in NFL history to throw 60 or more touchdown passes against multiple franchises.

But now, Rodgers is closing in on his final opportunities to add to that growing list of historic accomplishments.

Maybe it took him a couple of shots to reach the green, or maybe he took his time finding his shot on the fairway. Either way, the 18th hole is in sight, and Rodgers is crouched in front of his ball, squaring up the putt.

"I thought last year might be it," Rodgers said on the first day of training camp. "And then Mike [McCarthy] got hired. And I talked to the wife, and she said you can do one more year. I said, 'We'll see if it works out.' And it kind of all came together."

Among the milestones in reach for Rodgers are becoming the fourth quarterback in NFL history to appear in 300 games (as of Week 3 he has appeared in 290), joining Tom Brady (383), Favre (326) and Drew Brees (305), throwing the fourth-most touchdown passes in NFL history (as of Week 3, he has 531) and having the second-most regular-season games with multiple touchdown passes. And after Week 3, he needs 3,026 yards to become the fifth player to reach 70,000 passing yards. 

This season, we're chronicling Rodgers' individual milestones week by week as he rides his last rodeo and lines up his putt on the 18th green. Follow along here for the weekly installments.

Whom should you start? Whom should you sit? To help you set your fantasy football lineups and avoid starting an offensive player who won't be in the lineup, we'll post fantasy-relevant updates and analysis here as NFL teams release their official inactives lists. 

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 3 Buzz 

Week 3 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 3

Biggest concerns heading into Week 3

Players with early starts

ACTIVE

DJ Moore, WR, Bills (shoulder): Moore is active for Week 3. He has not missed a game since 2020. It should be noted that Moore was limited and wore a noncontact jersey twice during this past week, so while fantasy managers should plan to start him, he may be somewhat limited.

Keon Coleman, WR, Bills (ankle): Coleman also missed practice this week, but was able to log a limited session Friday and is active. However, that is more of a boost for Josh Allen and the Bills than it is fantasy managers.

Jalen Coker, WR, Panthers (ankle): After missing practice Thursday, Coker returned in a limited fashion Friday -- his second practice of the week. He is active for Week 3. He has seen nine targets in both games this season. In fact, his usage is very similar to Tetairoa McMillan, only Coker is seeing a higher number of efficient targets.

 Malik Nabers, WR, Giants (shoulder): Nabers suffered his injury during "Monday Night Football" but was able to return to the field. He did pop up on the practice report this week but was able to log in full practices and is active for Week 3. He is a more volatile fantasy option with Jameis Winston under center -- especially this week with bad weather.

In most weeks, Nabers should still be viewed as a fantasy WR2. However, given the conditions today, lower him to a WR3. I would rather go with DJ Moore, Jaylen Waddle, Ladd McConkey or Tee Higgins. Play Nabers over Emeka Egbuka, Terry McLaurin, DK Metcalf and Jameson Williams.

Michael Pittman Jr., WR, Steelers (foot): After missing Week 2, Pittman was able to log limited practices this week and is active for Week 3. Even so, Pittman is nothing more than a low-floor flex option due to the struggling Steelers passing attack. The list of streaming options mentioned above are all receivers I would rather play than Pittman.

Jadarian Price, RB, Seahawks (chest): Price was limited at practice to start the week but got in a full practice on Friday and is active for Week 3. The Seahawks face the Commanders, who have been "middle of the road" against RBs. However, game script should largely be on Seattle's side. As such, Price is an RB2 play who can be started over Travis Etienne Jr., Warren, Rhamondre Stevenson and any Broncos RB. Emanuel Wilson could still see touches after he turned 21 car

articles.headline: Vikings beat Buccaneers 23-16 but lose Jefferson to an ankle injury. Bucs' Mayfield also hurt
articles.description: — Myles Price returned a punt 86 yards for a score, Kyler Murray threw a 41-yard TD pass to Jordan Addison and the Minnesota Vikings beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 23-16 on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: バイキングスがバッカニアーズを23-16で破るもジェファーソンが足首負傷。バックスのメイフィールドも負傷
articles.descriptionJa: マイルズ・プライスが86ヤードのパントリターンタッチダウンを決め、カイラー・マレーがジョーダン・アディソンへ41ヤードのTDパスを通し、ミネソタ・バイキングスが日曜日にタンパベイ・バッカニアーズを23-16で破りました。
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- — Myles Price returned a punt 86 yards for a score, Kyler Murray threw a 41-yard TD pass to Jordan Addison and the Minnesota Vikings beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers 23-16 on Sunday.


              It was a costly game for both teams.


              Baker Mayfield hurt his thumb on a desperation pass late in the fourth quarter. He was screaming in pain on the ground before walking off and was replaced by rookie Jalon Daniels in the final minute.


              Two-time All-Pro wide receiver Justin Jefferson didn’t return for Minnesota after injuring his right ankle in the first quarter.


              The Vikings are 3-0 for the second time in three years. The Buccaneers are 0-3 for the first time since 2014, when they finished 2-14 and got the No. 1 overall draft pick, taking Jameis Winston.


              Murray was 15 of 29 for 168 yards with one TD pass and one interception in his first full game with the Vikings. He sustained a concussion in the first quarter of the season opener and Carson Wentz led Minnesota to consecutive wins.


              Mayfield hasn’t played like a $55 million-a-year quarterback since the Buccaneers gave him a $165 million extension before the season. He was 17 of 34 for 217 yards with one TD and one interception, taking six sacks.


              Tampa Bay’s woeful offense couldn’t do much against coordinator Brian Flores’ defense.


              Mayfield had an 85-yard touchdown pass to Chris Godwin Jr. on third-and-30 negated by a holding penalty on Luke Goedeke in the third quarter.


              That summed up the offense’s struggles.


              Mayfield’s 14-yard scramble on second-and-9 later was negated by a holding penalty on Payne Durham. But the Bucs got a first down on third-and-29 when Joshua Metellus hit Emeka Egbuka helmet-to-helmet. Again, the offense had to settle for a field goal. Chase McLauglin’s 54-yarder cut it to 17-16.


              Will Reichard’s 56-yard field goal extended Minnesota’s lead to 20-16 with 3:10 remaining. He added a 43-yarder to cap the scoring.


              Murray connected with Addison on a deep throw on third-and-8 to give the Vikings a 17-10 lead in the second quarter. Addison beat Jacob Parrish in one-on-one coverage, making a smooth adjustment on the ball.


              After A’Shawn Robinson intercepted Murray’s pass to set up a first down at the Vikings 22 in the third quarter, the Bucs went nowhere. Bucky Irving ran 3 yards and then dropped a pass. Mayfield got sacked on third down and McLaughlin’s 38-yarder cut it to 17-13.


              The Buccaneers fell behind 10-0 after just one possession. Following a three-and-out, Price darted up the middle, cut to the right and sprinted down the sideline for his first career touchdown.


              Mayfield fired a 40-yard TD pass down the seam to rookie Ted Hurst III to cut it to 10-7.
